q: The (Kriyâvâdins) Sramanas and Brâhmanas understanding the world (according to their lights), speak thus: misery is produced by one's own works, not by those of somebody else (viz. fate, creator, &c.). But right knowledge and conduct lead to liberation. (11)

s: Brâhmanas understand the world (according to their lights)
q: The (Kriyâvâdins) Sramanas and Brâhmanas understanding the world (according to their lights), speak thus: misery is produced by one's own works, not by those of somebody else (viz. fate, creator, &c.). But right knowledge and conduct lead to liberation. (11)

s: Akriyâvâdins is a heretical creed
q: There are four (heretical) creeds which the disputants severally uphold: 1. the Kriyâvâda, 2. the Akriyâvâda, 3. the Vinayavâda, and 4. the Agñânavâda. (1)

s: misery is produced by one's own works (not by those of somebody else)
q: The (Kriyâvâdins) Sramanas and Brâhmanas understanding the world (according to their lights), speak thus: misery is produced by one's own works, not by those of somebody else (viz. fate, creator, &c.). But right knowledge and conduct lead to liberation. (11)

s: right knowledge and conduct lead to final Liberation
q: But right knowledge and conduct lead to liberation. (11)

s: Tîrthakaras are eyes of the world (as it were)
q: The (Tîrthakaras), being (as it were) the eyes of the world and its leaders, teach the path which is salutary to men; they have declared that the world is eternal inasmuch as creatures are (for ever) living in it, O ye men! (12)

s: Tîrthakaras are leaders of the world
q: The (Tîrthakaras), being (as it were) the eyes of the world and its leaders, teach the path which is salutary to men; they have declared that the world is eternal inasmuch as creatures are (for ever) living in it, O ye men! (12)

s: Tîrthakaras teach path salutary to men
q: The (Tîrthakaras), being (as it were) the eyes of the world and its leaders, teach the path which is salutary to men; they have declared that the world is eternal inasmuch as creatures are (for ever) living in it, O ye men! (12)

s: the world is eternal eternal (because creatures are for ever living in it)
q: The (Tîrthakaras), being (as it were) the eyes of the world and its leaders, teach the path which is salutary to men; they have declared that the world is eternal inasmuch as creatures are (for ever) living in it, O ye men! (12)

s: living beings are reborn again and again
q: The Râkshasas and the dwellers in Yama's world, the troops of Asuras and Gandharvas, and the spirits that walk the air, and individual beings: they will all be born again and again. (13)

s: Samsâra is compared to boundless flood of water
q: The Samsâra) which is compared to the boundless flood of water, know it to be impassable and of very long duration on account of repeated births

s: Samsâra is impassable (on account of repeated births)
q: The Samsâra) which is compared to the boundless flood of water, know it to be impassable and of very long duration on account of repeated births

s: Samsâra has duration very long (on account of repeated births)
q: The Samsâra) which is compared to the boundless flood of water, know it to be impassable and of very long duration on account of repeated births

s: Vinayavâda is a heretical creed
q: There are four (heretical) creeds which the disputants severally uphold: 1. the Kriyâvâda, 2. the Akriyâvâda, 3. the Vinayavâda, and 4. the Agñânavâda. (1)

s: monk annihilate works (by abstention from works)
q: The sinners cannot annihilate their works by new works; the pious annihilate their works by abstention from works; the wise and happy men who got rid of the effects of greed, do not commit sins. (15)

s: monk are averse to injury of living beings
q: Averse to injury of living beings, they do not act, nor cause others to act. Always restraining themselves, those pious men practise control, and some become heroes through their knowledge. (17)

s: monk practise control (always restraining themselves)
q: Averse to injury of living beings, they do not act, nor cause others to act. Always restraining themselves, those pious men practise control, and some become heroes through their knowledge. (17)

s: heroes arise from monk (through their knowledge)
q: Averse to injury of living beings, they do not act, nor cause others to act. Always restraining themselves, those pious men practise control, and some become heroes through their knowledge. (17)

s: Law is made manifest by men who have learned the truth (after having well considered it)
q: One should always honour a man, who is like a light and makes manifest the Law after having well considered it. (19)

s: control guards from Circle of Births
q: Being not attached to sounds and colours, indifferent to tastes and smells, not desiring life nor death, guarded by control, and exempt from the Circle (of Births). (22)

s: Agñânavâda is a heretical creed
q: There are four (heretical) creeds which the disputants severally uphold: 1. the Kriyâvâda, 2. the Akriyâvâda, 3. the Vinayavâda, and 4. the Agñânavâda. (1)

s: agnostics reason incoherently (though they pretend to be clever)
q: The agnostics, though they (pretend to) be clever, reason incoherently, and do not get beyond the confusion of their ideas

s: agnostics remain in confusion of their ideas
q: The agnostics, though they (pretend to) be clever, reason incoherently, and do not get beyond the confusion of their ideas

s: Vinayavâda is upheld by various upholders of Vinaya
q: Believing truth to be untruth, and calling a bad man good, the various upholders of Vinaya, asked about it, explain their tenet. (3)

s: Thirteenth Lecture, Called the Real Truth is a lecture
q: Thirteenth Lecture, Called the Real Truth.

s: men falsify Law (when explaining it according to individual opinion)
q: Those who explain the pure doctrine according to their individual opinion, falsify it in repeating (it after their teachers);

s: men speak untruth untruth (from pride of knowledge)
q: those who speak untruth from pride of knowledge, are not capable of many virtues.

s: men conceal truth (when questioned)
q: Those who on being questioned conceal the truth, defraud themselves of the real good.

s: men are quarrelsome (when talking improperly)
q: He who is quarrelsome and talks improperly, is not impartial nor beyond the reach of deceit;

s: men are not beyond reach of deceit (when quarrelsome and talking improperly)
q: He who is quarrelsome and talks improperly, is not impartial nor beyond the reach of deceit;

s: men have qualities various (in accordance with truth)
q: I shall now expound, in accordance with truth, the various qualities of men;

s: men execute commands of teacher (while controlling themselves)
q: but he who executes the commands (of his teacher) and controls himself, sees nothing but the truth and is exempt from deceit.

s: men are exempt from deceit (when executing the teacher's commands and controlling themselves)
q: but he who executes the commands (of his teacher) and controls himself, sees nothing but the truth and is exempt from deceit.

s: men conform to admonitions (however many they receive)
q: He who conforms to admonitions however many he receives, is kindly spoken, subtile, manly, noble, and a well-doer;

s: men are impartial impartial (when conforming to admonitions)
q: (such a man) is impartial and beyond the reach of deceit.

s: men are beyond reach of deceit (when conforming to admonitions)
q: (such a man) is impartial and beyond the reach of deceit.

s: Gôtra is a place for Vow of Silence (where it is practised)
q: He is always turned round by delusion, and has no place in the Gôtra where the Vow of Silence is practised

s: Vow of Silence is practised in Gaina church
q: where the Vow of Silence is practised (viz. in the Gaina church),

s: Gôtra is part of Gaina church (as the place where the Vow of Silence is practised)
q: has no place in the Gôtra where the Vow of Silence is practised (viz. in the Gaina church),

s: Ugra race has scion monk (among those entering the order)
q: a scion of the Ugra race or a Likkhavi, who enters the order eating alms given him by others,

s: monk eat alms (given by others)
q: who enters the order eating alms given him by others,

s: monk require right knowledge and conduct (rather than pedigree)
q: His pedigree on his mother's and on his father's side will be of no use to him, nothing will but right knowledge and conduct:

s: monk act like householder (after becoming a monk)
q: when after becoming a monk he acts like a householder,

s: householder prevents final Liberation (when a monk acts like one after ordination)
q: when after becoming a monk he acts like a householder, he will not succeed in obtaining final Liberation.

s: monk fail to obtain final Liberation (when acting like householders)
q: when after becoming a monk he acts like a householder, he will not succeed in obtaining final Liberation.

s: monk suffer in Circle of Births (when attached to vanities and fame and using monkhood as a means of subsistence)
q: If a poor monk subsisting on the meanest food is attached to vanities, desires fame, and not being awakened, (makes his monkhood) a means of subsistence, he will suffer again and again (in the Circle of Births).

s: monk are eloquent eloquent (in the case of an intellectually gifted monk)
q: A monk, who is eloquent, speaks very well, has bright ideas, is clever, possesses a fine intellect, and has purified his soul,

s: sinners have vices and unrest
q: I shall now expound, in accordance with truth, the various qualities of men; I shall explain the virtue and peace of the good, the vices and the unrest of the wicked.

s: monk may despise men (on account of intellect)
q: may (perhaps) despise other men on account of his intellect.

s: monk combat pride (of genius, sanctity, birth, and good living)
q: A monk should combat pride of genius, pride of sanctity, pride of birth, and (pride of good) living, which is enumerated as the fourth;

s: great sages are above Gôtra (and similar distinctions)
q: the great sages are above all such things as Gôtra (&c.),

s: great sages ascend to Môksha (beyond all Gôtra distinctions)
q: and they ascend to the place where there is no Gôtra at all (viz. to Môksha).

s: monk look upon body (as on a corpse)
q: A monk who looks upon his body as on a corpse and fully understands the Law,

s: monk understand Law (fully)
q: A monk who looks upon his body as on a corpse and fully understands the Law,

s: monk distinguish food and drink (in a village or town, between what may be accepted and what may not)
q: will on entering a village or a town distinguish between what may be accepted and what may not, and will not be greedy of food or drink.

s: Tathâgatas teach Law (through men who exert themselves day and night)
q: Having learned the Law from men who exert themselves day and night, from the Tathâgatas,

s: monk are not greedy of food and drink
q: and will not be greedy of food or drink.

s: monk conquer aversion to control (while living in company or alone)
q: A monk having conquered aversion to control and delight in sensual objects, living in company with many brethren or leading a single life,

s: monk conquer sensual objects (by overcoming delight in them)
q: A monk having conquered aversion to control and delight in sensual objects, living in company with many brethren or leading a single life,

s: monk repeat a man must come and go according to his Karman alone (silently to themselves)
q: should silently repeat to himself: 'A man must come and go (according to his Karman) alone' (i.e. without deriving any help from others).

s: monk teach Law (when knowing it by intuition or having learned it from others)
q: Knowing it by intuition or having learned it from others, one should teach the Law which is a benefit to men;

s: Law benefits men
q: one should teach the Law which is a benefit to men;

s: monk may be wounded by men (when preaching to someone whose disposition is unknown and who becomes angry)
q: that man, not believing (what he is taught), will become angry, and may wound him in a way that will shorten or end his life.

s: men learn Law (from Tathâgatas through men who exert themselves day and night)
q: Having learned the Law from men who exert themselves day and night, from the Tathâgatas,

s: men come to harm through sensual objects (objects of sight or senses)
q: For) through the objects of sight (i.e. senses) which are causes of danger, men come to harm.

s: monk should not desire honour or fame
q: Not desiring honour or fame, he should say nothing to anybody either to please or to irritate him.

s: monk preach Law (without embarrassment and passion, avoiding all evils)
q: Avoiding all evils, a monk should without embarrassment and passion (preach the Law).

s: monk abstain from injuring living beings (in accordance with truth)
q: Well considering (his duties) in accordance with truth, abstaining from doing injury to living beings, not desiring life nor death,

s: living beings are not to be injured by monk (as a matter of duty)
q: Well considering (his duties) in accordance with truth, abstaining from doing injury to living beings,

s: monk do not desire life nor death (while wandering released from the Circle of Births)
q: not desiring life nor death, he should wander about released from the Circle (of Births).

s: monk are released from Circle of Births (while wandering without desiring life or death)
q: he should wander about released from the Circle (of Births).

s: men neglect conduct (after being instructed in it)
q: they neglect the conduct in which they had been instructed,

s: men speak rudely to teacher
q: and speak rudely to their teacher.

s: teacher is spoken to rudely by they (when they neglect the conduct in which they had been instructed)
q: they neglect the conduct in which they had been instructed, and speak rudely to their teacher.

s: monk is instructed in creed (after giving up worldly ties)
q: He who has given up all worldly ties and is instructed in our creed, should practise chastity, exerting himself; obeying the commands (of his teacher) he should make himself well acquainted with the conduct; a clever (monk) should avoid carelessness. (1)

s: monk lives with teacher (to perform his duties and end mundane existence)
q: A good man should long to live with his teacher in order to perform his duties, knowing that he who does not live with his teacher will not put an end to his mundane existence. Making manifest the conduct of the virtuous, an intelligent (monk) should not leave the (company of his teacher). (4)

s: monk follows Yatis (regarding postures, lying down, sitting, and exertions)
q: (A monk) who complies with the rules for Yatis as regards postures, lying down, sitting, and exertions, who is thoroughly acquainted with the Samitis and Guptis, should in teaching others explain each single (point of conduct). (5)

s: monk is acquainted with Samitis (thoroughly)
q: (A monk) who complies with the rules for Yatis as regards postures, lying down, sitting, and exertions, who is thoroughly acquainted with the Samitis and Guptis, should in teaching others explain each single (point of conduct). (5)

s: monk is acquainted with Guptis (thoroughly)
q: (A monk) who complies with the rules for Yatis as regards postures, lying down, sitting, and exertions, who is thoroughly acquainted with the Samitis and Guptis, should in teaching others explain each single (point of conduct). (5)

s: monk perseveres in control (regardless of pleasant or dreadful sounds)
q: Whether he hears (pleasant) sounds or dreadful ones, he should not allow himself to be influenced by them, and persevere in control; nor should a monk be sleepy or careless, but by every means he should get rid of doubts. (6)

s: monk gets rid of doubts (by every means)
q: Whether he hears (pleasant) sounds or dreadful ones, he should not allow himself to be influenced by them, and persevere in control; nor should a monk be sleepy or careless, but by every means he should get rid of doubts. (6)

s: monk is free from passion (when admonished)
q: If admonished by a young or an old monk, by one above him or one of equal age, he should not retort against him, being perfectly free from passion; for one who is (as it were) carried away (by the stream of the Samsâra), will not get to its opposite shore. (7)

s: monk does not harm living beings (when corrected by others)
q: He should not be angry with them nor do them any harm, nor say a single hard word to them, but he should promise not to commit the same sin again; for this is better than to do wrong. (9)

s: monk does not commit sin (again after correction)
q: He should not be angry with them nor do them any harm, nor say a single hard word to them, but he should promise not to commit the same sin again; for this is better than to do wrong. (9)

s: monk practises chastity (exerting himself)
q: He who has given up all worldly ties and is instructed in our creed, should practise chastity, exerting himself; obeying the commands (of his teacher) he should make himself well acquainted with the conduct; a clever (monk) should avoid carelessness. (1)

s: monk is restrained with regard to living beings (movable and immovable beings on high, below, and on earth)
q: Always restrained with regard to movable and immovable beings which are on high, below, and on earth, (a monk) should wander about entertaining no hostile thoughts (towards them) and being steadfast (in control). (14)

s: monk entertains no hostile thoughts towards living beings (while wandering)
q: Always restrained with regard to movable and immovable beings which are on high, below, and on earth, (a monk) should wander about entertaining no hostile thoughts (towards them) and being steadfast (in control). (14)

s: monk follows Law (after hearing it from a well-conducted monk)
q: At the right time he may put a question about living beings to a well-conducted (monk), who will explain the conduct of the virtuous; and what he hears he should follow and treasure up in his heart, thinking that it is the doctrine of the Kêvalins. (15)

s: monk protects living beings (in thoughts, words, and acts)
q: Living in this (company of the teacher) and protecting (himself or other beings) in the three ways (viz. in thoughts, words, and acts), he (gets) peace and the annihilation (of sins) as they say. Thus speak those who know the three worlds, and they do not again commit faults! (16)

s: monk hears Truth (the desired Truth)
q: A monk by hearing the desired Truth gets bright ideas and becomes a clever (teacher); desiring the highest good and practising austerities and silence, he will obtain final Liberation (living on) pure (food). (17)

s: monk practises austerities (desiring the highest good)
q: A monk by hearing the desired Truth gets bright ideas and becomes a clever (teacher); desiring the highest good and practising austerities and silence, he will obtain final Liberation (living on) pure (food). (17)

s: monk practises silence (desiring the highest good)
q: A monk by hearing the desired Truth gets bright ideas and becomes a clever (teacher); desiring the highest good and practising austerities and silence, he will obtain final Liberation (living on) pure (food). (17)

s: monk obtains final Liberation (through austerities and silence)
q: A monk by hearing the desired Truth gets bright ideas and becomes a clever (teacher); desiring the highest good and practising austerities and silence, he will obtain final Liberation (living on) pure (food). (17)

s: monk does not conceal Truth (as a wise interpreter)
q: He does not conceal (the truth) nor falsify it; he should not indulge his pride and (desire for) fame; being wise he should not joke, nor pronounce benedictions. (19)

s: monk obeys teacher (the teacher's commands)
q: He who has given up all worldly ties and is instructed in our creed, should practise chastity, exerting himself; obeying the commands (of his teacher) he should make himself well acquainted with the conduct; a clever (monk) should avoid carelessness. (1)

s: monk does not falsify Truth (as a wise interpreter)
q: He does not conceal (the truth) nor falsify it; he should not indulge his pride and (desire for) fame; being wise he should not joke, nor pronounce benedictions. (19)

s: monk does not use spells (as a good man)
q: Averse to injury of living beings, he does not disgrace his calling by the use of spells; a good man does not desire anything from other people, and he does not give utterance to heretical doctrines. (20)

s: monk does not give utterance to heretical doctrines (as a good man)
q: Averse to injury of living beings, he does not disgrace his calling by the use of spells; a good man does not desire anything from other people, and he does not give utterance to heretical doctrines. (20)

s: monk is single single (living alone)
q: A monk living single should not ridicule heretical doctrines, and should avoid hard words though they be true; he should not be vain, nor brag, but he should without embarrassment and passion (preach the Law). (21)

s: monk expounds Syâdvâda (modestly and fearlessly)
q: A monk should be modest though he be of a fearless mind; he should expound the Syâdvâda; he should use the two (permitted) kinds of speech, living among virtuous men, impartial and wise. (22)

s: monk is impartial (living among virtuous men)
q: A monk should be modest though he be of a fearless mind; he should expound the Syâdvâda; he should use the two (permitted) kinds of speech, living among virtuous men, impartial and wise. (22)

s: monk is wise (living among virtuous men)
q: A monk should be modest though he be of a fearless mind; he should expound the Syâdvâda; he should use the two (permitted) kinds of speech, living among virtuous men, impartial and wise. (22)

s: monk uses speech (the two permitted kinds)
q: A monk should be modest though he be of a fearless mind; he should expound the Syâdvâda; he should use the two (permitted) kinds of speech, living among virtuous men, impartial and wise. (22)

s: monk declares sin (distinguishing sin in pure speech)
q: When the pupil has heard it, he will correctly understand the Truth. A monk should utter pure speech, which is in accordance with the creed (of the Ginas), and should declare the distinction of sin. (24)

s: monk is devoted to teacher (delivering faithfully what he has learned)
q: He should not pervert nor render obscure (the truth); he should fabricate neither text nor meaning, being a saviour; being devoted to the Teacher and considering well his words, he delivers faithfully what he has learned. (26)

s: monk avoids carelessness (as a clever monk)
q: He who has given up all worldly ties and is instructed in our creed, should practise chastity, exerting himself; obeying the commands (of his teacher) he should make himself well acquainted with the conduct; a clever (monk) should avoid carelessness. (1)

s: monk is competent to explain creed (when authentic, clever, learned, and versed in the Law)
q: He who correctly knows the sacred texts, who practises austerities, who understands all details of the Law, who is an authentic interpreter, clever, and learned--such a man is competent to explain the entire creed. (27)

s: creed is in accordance with Ginas (in pure speech)
q: When the pupil has heard it, he will correctly understand the Truth. A monk should utter pure speech, which is in accordance with the creed (of the Ginas), and should declare the distinction of sin. (24)

s: novice knows Law (after hearing the words of the Ginas)
q: So a novice who has not mastered the Law, does not know the Law, not being awakened; but afterwards he knows it well through the words of the Ginas, as with his eye (the wanderer sees the way) after sunrise. (13)

s: Ginas awaken novice (through their words)
q: So a novice who has not mastered the Law, does not know the Law, not being awakened; but afterwards he knows it well through the words of the Ginas, as with his eye (the wanderer sees the way) after sunrise. (13)

s: Truth gives bright ideas (when heard by a monk)
q: A monk by hearing the desired Truth gets bright ideas and becomes a clever (teacher); desiring the highest good and practising austerities and silence, he will obtain final Liberation (living on) pure (food). (17)

s: unprincipled men seduce novice (when the novice has not yet mastered the Law and has left the Gakkha)
q: Just as they carry off a young bird whose wings are not yet grown, so many unprincipled men will seduce a novice who has not yet mastered the Law, thinking that they can get him in their power, when they have made him leave (the Gakkha). (3)

s: novice has not mastered Law (before being fully instructed)
q: Just as they carry off a young bird whose wings are not yet grown, so many unprincipled men will seduce a novice who has not yet mastered the Law, thinking that they can get him in their power, when they have made him leave (the Gakkha). (3)
